q1.boundary: The broker boundary of the Catalog Management bounded context. Its two services move their Kafka client (producer and consumers) from Redpanda (redpanda:29092) to Apache Kafka (kafka:29092). Every other service stays on Redpanda, including ecommerce-tenant-service (store-provisioning) and the product and category query services. So every consumer x topic binding between Catalog Management and another context becomes a broker crossing that MirrorMaker 2 must bridge. Bindings with both ends inside Catalog Management (ecommerce-image-service on catalog.product.events) move together and need no mirror.

q4.must_preserve: Every ProductUpdated/ProductDeleted event from the catalog service and every ProductImagePromoted event from the image service, both produced on Kafka after the move, must reach the Redpanda topic of the same name. This needs Kafka->Redpanda mirroring with the topic name unchanged. The group's existing Redpanda offset (120) must stay valid: mirrored records are appended after it, and the topic is not recreated or reset. Without this, the storefront product read model and image URLs go stale.

evidence.reference: declared event types ProductImagePromoted, ProductUpdated for this binding

q4.must_preserve: AttributeUpdated events produced on Kafka must reach Redpanda catalog.attribute.events under the same name. Product events carry only attribute ids and slugs, and the query service joins attribute display data from this stream. This binding is undocumented and has no catalog promise, so a plan built only from the documents or the AIP promises would miss it.
CategoryUpdated events produced on Kafka must reach Redpanda catalog.category.events under the same name and after the group's committed offset (4), so the category read model keeps getting updates.

The same catalog.attribute.events mirror flow as for the product query service; it must also keep this second consumer group fed (offset 20). Undocumented, so it must not be dropped from the allow-list.

TenantUpdated/TenantDeleted events from ecommerce-tenant-service, which stays on Redpanda, must reach Kafka tenant.tenant.events (Redpanda->Kafka mirror). The group's position must carry over (MM2 offset sync), so new tenants are not missed and old ones are not reprocessed if avoidable. The handler runs per-tenant database migrations on TenantUpdated and cleanup on TenantDeleted; a missed event leaves a new tenant without migrated catalog collections.

The same Redpanda->Kafka flow and offset carry-over for group ecommerce-image-service. Its tenant handler also runs the S3 tenant cleaner on TenantDeleted (wiping the tenant's image prefix), so a missed delete leaves the tenant's objects in place, and a redelivered one repeats the cleanup.

q5.statement: Delivery between the brokers is not established by any evidence. AIP says it never establishes it. After the move, verify that the Kafka end-offset growth of each catalog topic equals the Redpanda growth, that the query-service groups advance with lag 0, and that the functional test passes. MM2 is at-least-once: duplicates (and possibly reordering across the cutover) can occur. This plan makes no lossless or exactly-once claim.
